title: Building Self-Control with AI
subject: AI-Literacy
description: Comprehensive practice on using self-control with AI: the ripple effect of AI misuse, weighing personal vs community impact, choosing responsible paths over shortcuts, the power-responsibility connection, and a real-world AI voice-cloning scam.

questions.topic: The Big Question: Does AI Always Get to Decide?
questions.question: What is the title of this AI-Literacy chapter?
options: Building Self-Control with AI
Building Trust with Robots
Learning to Code with AI
Making Friends with AI
questions.explanation: The chapter is titled 'Building Self-Control with AI' and focuses on pausing to think before letting AI act for you.

questions.topic: The Big Question: Does AI Always Get to Decide?
questions.question: What question opens this chapter's worksheet?
options: Just because AI can do it for you, should you always let it?
How fast can AI finish your homework?
What is your favourite AI app?
How much does AI cost?
questions.explanation: The worksheet opens with 'Just because AI can do it for you, should you always let it?' — the core question behind self-control with AI.

questions.topic: The Big Question: Does AI Always Get to Decide?
questions.question: The worksheet's opening question suggests that just because AI CAN do something for you, you should always let it.
questions.explanation: The question is asked precisely to make students doubt this idea — being able to do something is not the same as it being the right choice.

questions.topic: The Big Question: Does AI Always Get to Decide?
questions.question: What does 'self-control' mean when using AI, based on this chapter?
options: Choosing wisely whether to use AI, even when you could
Using AI as much as possible
Letting AI make every decision for you
Never touching AI at all
questions.explanation: Self-control means pausing to think and choosing responsibly, not simply avoiding AI or using it for everything.

questions.topic: The Big Question: Does AI Always Get to Decide?
questions.question: Why does the chapter ask 'should you always let it?' rather than just 'can AI do it?'
options: Because being able to do something is not the same as it being the right choice
Because AI can never actually do anything
Because asking twice is required by law
Because 'can' and 'should' mean exactly the same thing
questions.explanation: The chapter separates ABILITY (can AI do it) from RESPONSIBILITY (should you let it), which is the heart of self-control.

questions.topic: The Big Question: Does AI Always Get to Decide?
questions.question: Just because something is possible with AI, it is automatically the responsible choice.
questions.explanation: Possibility and responsibility are different — this chapter's scenarios (like Rahul's fake clip) show that possible actions can still be harmful.

questions.topic: The Big Question: Does AI Always Get to Decide?
questions.question: Which word best describes stopping yourself from using AI in a way that could cause harm?
options: Self-control
Carelessness
Curiosity
Speed
questions.explanation: Self-control is the skill of pausing and choosing not to act, even when you are able to.

questions.topic: The Big Question: Does AI Always Get to Decide?
questions.question: Select ALL statements that reflect the idea behind 'Just because AI can do it for you, should you always let it?'
options: AI's ability to do a task doesn't make it the right choice
You should think before letting AI act for you
If AI can do something, you must always use it that way
Self-control means pausing to consider consequences
questions.explanation: The question challenges the idea that AI's ability equals permission — it asks students to pause, think, and consider consequences.

questions.topic: The Big Question: Does AI Always Get to Decide?
questions.question: A student says, 'AI can write my whole essay, so I should let it do everything.' What is missing from this thinking?
options: Self-control and thinking about whether that's the responsible choice
Nothing — this is correct
The essay would be worse if AI helped
AI cannot write essays
questions.explanation: The student confuses 'AI can' with 'I should' — exactly the trap this chapter warns against.

questions.topic: The Big Question: Does AI Always Get to Decide?
questions.question: This chapter's activities mainly focus on building which single skill?
options: Self-control while using AI
Spelling
Drawing
Calculating quickly
questions.explanation: Every activity in the worksheet — Rahul's clip, the ranking task, Keya's report, the spectrum, and the case study — builds self-control with AI.

questions.topic: The Big Question: Does AI Always Get to Decide?
questions.question: What kind of tool is AI described as in this chapter?
options: A powerful tool that needs responsible use
A toy with no real effects
Something that can only help, never harm
A tool only teachers can use
questions.explanation: The worksheet describes AI as a powerful tool, which is exactly why responsible, self-controlled use matters.

questions.topic: The Big Question: Does AI Always Get to Decide?
questions.question: Which of these is the best example of practicing self-control with AI?
options: Pausing before sharing an AI-made post to think about who could be affected
Sharing anything AI makes immediately
Letting AI post to social media without checking
Never thinking about consequences
questions.explanation: Self-control means pausing to think about impact BEFORE acting, not acting immediately or without thought.

questions.topic: The Big Question: Does AI Always Get to Decide?
questions.question: Which is the tempting-but-wrong belief this chapter warns against?
options: ‘If AI can generate it, it's fine to share it right away’
‘I should think before I let AI act’
‘Some AI actions need self-control’
‘Not every AI action is a good idea’
questions.explanation: The other three options ARE the chapter's actual lessons; the first is the mistaken belief the chapter tries to correct.

questions.topic: The Big Question: Does AI Always Get to Decide?
questions.question: Self-control with AI only matters for grown-ups, not for students.
questions.explanation: Every scenario in this chapter — Rahul, Keya, and the spectrum activity — is about students practicing self-control with AI.

questions.topic: The Big Question: Does AI Always Get to Decide?
questions.question: This chapter includes real scenarios and a real news case study to teach self-control with AI.
questions.explanation: The chapter uses Rahul's and Keya's scenarios plus a real ABC News case study about AI voice cloning.

questions.topic: Ripple Effect: Rahul's Fake Audio Clip

questions.topic: Ripple Effect: Rahul's Fake Audio Clip
questions.question: Select ALL that are true about Rahul's actions.

The clip falsely accused the winning team of cheating
He shared the fake clip with the school sports group
He created the clip because his team won the match

questions.topic: Ripple Effect: Rahul's Fake Audio Clip

Thinking deeper
Learning is Fun

questions.topic: Ripple Effect: Rahul's Fake Audio Clip

options: The ripple
The domino theory
The chain of command
The feedback loop

questions.topic: Ripple Effect: Rahul's Fake Audio Clip

options: Who gets pulled in, and how it affects them
Only how much money is lost
Only what Rahul feels
Nothing — the rings are just decoration

questions.topic: Ripple Effect: Rahul's Fake Audio Clip
questions.question: Which ring would most likely include the people closest to and most immediately affected by Rahul's fake clip, like the rival coach?
options: Ring 1
Ring 2
Ring 3
None of the rings
questions.explanation: Ring 1 is the innermost ring, representing the people most directly and immediately affected — here, the falsely accused rival coach.

questions.topic: Ripple Effect: Rahul's Fake Audio Clip
questions.question: As you move from Ring 1 to Ring 3 in the ripple model, what generally happens to the fake clip's reach?
options: It reaches more and more people, farther from the original action
It reaches fewer and fewer people
It disappears completely
It becomes true
questions.explanation: Like ripples in water, the effect spreads outward to reach a wider group of people the farther out you go.

questions.topic: Self-Control Checkpoints
questions.question: Select ALL the moments the worksheet lists as possible stopping points for Rahul's ripple effect.
options: Before creating it
Before sharing it
After sharing it
Before the match started
questions.explanation: The worksheet's self-control check offers exactly these three moments: before creating it, before sharing it, and after sharing it.

questions.topic: Self-Control Checkpoints
questions.question: According to the self-control lesson, which is the EARLIEST — and best — moment Rahul could have stopped the harm?
options: Before creating the fake clip
Before sharing the clip
After sharing the clip
During the match
questions.explanation: Stopping before creating the clip prevents it from ever existing, stopping every ring of the ripple at once. The other moments are later, when some harm may already be unavoidable.

questions.topic: Self-Control Checkpoints
questions.question: Waiting until 'after sharing it' to feel bad about the fake clip would have prevented the school sports group from ever seeing it.
questions.explanation: Once something is shared, it usually cannot be un-shared or un-seen — self-control has to happen before the harmful action, not after.

questions.topic: Self-Control Checkpoints
questions.question: Since both 'stop before creating it' and 'stop before sharing it' would keep the clip out of the sports group, they are equally good choices with no real difference.
questions.explanation: 'Before creating it' is safer and earlier — the harmful audio never exists at all, so there is no risk of it leaking, being copied, or being shared later by mistake or by someone else.

questions.topic: Self-Control Checkpoints
questions.question: What could Rahul have done instead of creating the fake clip?
options: Talk about his frustration honestly, without creating false content
Create the clip but not tell anyone
Share the clip privately only
Create more fake clips
questions.explanation: Self-control means channelling anger into honest, harmless responses instead of creating deceptive content.

questions.topic: Ripple Effect: Rahul's Fake Audio Clip

questions.topic: Ripple Effect: Rahul's Fake Audio Clip

It made the match results officially change
questions.explanation: A fake accusation cannot change official match results, but it can still cause reputational and social harm.

questions.topic: Ripple Effect: Rahul's Fake Audio Clip
questions.question: An AI-generated audio clip that sounds exactly like a real person is still fake if that person never actually said those words.
questions.explanation: Sounding real does not make content true — it is still a fabricated, fake clip.

questions.topic: Ripple Effect: Rahul's Fake Audio Clip
questions.question: Someone argues, 'It's not a big deal, it's just audio, not a real recording.' What is wrong with this thinking?
options: A convincing fake can cause just as much real harm as a genuine recording, because people believe it
Audio can never cause harm
Only videos can be fake
Fake audio is always obviously fake
questions.explanation: People often trust what they hear; a convincing fake voice clip can spread false belief and harm just as effectively as a real recording.

options: Strong emotions like anger can tempt people to misuse AI to hurt others
Anger has nothing to do with AI misuse
AI cannot be used when you are angry
You should always act on anger immediately
questions.explanation: Rahul's anger about losing the match tempted him to misuse AI — showing why self-control matters most in emotional moments.

questions.explanation: Rahul was angry because his team LOST the inter-school match, not because they won.

questions.topic: Ripple Effect: Rahul's Fake Audio Clip

options: A single AI-made action can spread and affect many people beyond the person who made it
AI actions only affect the person who created them
Ripples in ponds have nothing to do with AI

questions.explanation: The ripple metaphor shows how one action (Rahul's fake clip) can spread outward to affect more and more people.

options: Whether the impact is Low, Medium, or High
Whether it is legal or illegal
The exact number of people affected
The colour of the AI tool
questions.explanation: The worksheet asks students to 'tick whether the impact is Low / Medium / High.'

questions.topic: Ranking the Impact of AI Actions
questions.question: Which of these four situations most likely affects the FEWEST people?
options: Using AI to complete your own personal diary entry
Using AI to write a class announcement without checking accuracy
Sharing a friend's address with an AI travel app without asking
Using AI to spread a rumour about a group of learners
questions.explanation: A personal diary entry is meant only for the writer, so it affects the fewest people of the four situations.

questions.topic: Ranking the Impact of AI Actions
questions.question: Why does a personal diary entry likely have LOW impact?
options: Because it is meant only for yourself and does not reach other people
Because diary entries are always false
Because AI cannot write diary entries
Because it involves many people
questions.explanation: A private diary entry stays with the writer, so it has the smallest reach of the four situations.

questions.topic: Ranking the Impact of AI Actions
questions.question: Why could using AI to write a class announcement WITHOUT checking accuracy be riskier than a diary entry?
options: A whole class could read incorrect information, spreading a mistake
It is exactly as private as a diary
No one reads class announcements
AI cannot make mistakes in announcements
questions.explanation: An announcement is shared with a whole class, so an unchecked mistake can mislead many people at once.

questions.topic: Ranking the Impact of AI Actions
questions.question: Why is sharing a friend's address with an AI travel app WITHOUT asking a serious concern?
options: It shares someone else's private and personal information without their permission
It only affects the person sharing it
Travel apps never store information
Addresses are public information anyway
questions.explanation: An address is private information belonging to the friend, so sharing it without asking violates their privacy.

questions.topic: Ranking the Impact of AI Actions
questions.question: Why does using AI to spread a rumour about a group of learners likely have HIGH impact?
options: It can unfairly hurt the reputation and feelings of many people at once
It only affects one person
Rumours have no real effect on people
It is the same as writing a private diary entry
questions.explanation: A rumour about a GROUP means many people can be hurt at once, making it the highest-impact situation listed.

questions.topic: Ranking the Impact of AI Actions

Sharing a friend's address with an AI travel app without asking
Using AI to spread a rumour about a group of learners
Using AI to write a class announcement without checking if it's accurate
questions.explanation: A diary entry is only about yourself; the other three situations can affect other people's privacy, reputation, or access to accurate information.

questions.topic: Ranking the Impact of AI Actions
questions.question: Which situation is LEAST like the others because it stays entirely personal?

questions.explanation: The diary entry is a private action that does not reach or affect other people, unlike the other three.

questions.topic: Ranking the Impact of AI Actions

questions.topic: Ranking the Impact of AI Actions

questions.topic: Ranking the Impact of AI Actions
